w:r.w:t: Blue Carbon Finance for Pacific Fisheries
Feasibility assessment for a blended finance facility supporting coastal communities
A blended finance facility can mobilise private capital for community fisheries if concessional funding absorbs the first losses.
Private capital mobilised per USD of concessional funding
Coastal communities in the first phase

The facility would lend to community fisheries cooperatives against verified blue carbon outcomes. The structure has three tiers: a first-loss grant tranche, a concessional debt tranche and a commercial senior tranche. Each tier has a clear owner and a defined return.
Capital is not the binding constraint. Coordination, bankability and verification are.

Pacific coastal ecosystems store large quantities of carbon, but most community-led conservation is funded by short grants. Investors lack a standard way to price the risk, and communities lack the technical capacity to prepare bankable projects.
many small grants, none large enough to finance infrastructure.
verification methods differ between donors and registries.
project preparation is slow and costly.
Lowers the blended cost of capital
A steering committee of funders and community representatives approves each project. The facility manager reports to the committee every quarter
“The real failure is one of coordination, bankability and structuring capacity.”
